Intrathecal pump: bulky, expensive, requires revision. CereVasc IP US11850390B2 + US11883309B2: MUST be checked for anticipation (G02). Systemic + BBB-opening: off-target exposure. H2 not fully refuted: CereVasc's own IP must be checked for anticipation (this is a G02 gate, not G09). Conclusion: G09 moves from RED to YELLOW. Strongest-alternative attack is INCOMPLETE pending G02 review of CereVasc IP US11850390B2 + US11883309B2.

experiments_executed.result: CEMETERY_CONSULTATION_COMPLETE. 2 retention-related entries consulted (CE-002 multi-mechanism retention, CE-003 large-payload size-selective retention). CE-003 is PROVEN_INVARIANT: CSF turnover rate (2.88x/day = 259 turnovers in 90 days) makes membrane-based retention physically impossible. C3 MUST NOT use membrane-based retention. C3's V8.8 mechanism is CONTROLLED retention (active release), not passive membrane. Per CE-003: 'CSF turnover rate makes it physically impossible for any membrane or affinity mechanism.' C3's controlled mechanism is NOT a membrane/affinity mechanism — it is an active release mechanism. No CE violation. However, C3 must demonstrate that controlled release can sustain concentration above therapeutic threshold despite 2.88x/day turnover. This requires analytical derivation (C3-E03) and parameter sweep (C3-E04).

experiments_executed.description: Derive steady-state concentration vs CSF turnover rate analytically — confirm controlled retention mechanism can sustain concentration above therapeutic threshold
experiments_executed.discriminates: H1 vs H3 (does the math support sustained concentration?)
experiments_executed.result: ANALYTICAL_DERIVATION_COMPLETE. Steady-state concentration C_ss under CSF turnover: C_ss = (release_rate R) / (CSF_turnover_rate × V_CSF) where V_CSF ≈ 150 mL, CSF_turnover_rate = 2.88/day = 0.002/s. For therapeutic concentration C_therapeutic (e.g., 1 nM for monoclonal antibody): R_required = C_therapeutic × 0.002/s × 150e-3 L = 3e-4 nmol/s = 26 nmol/day. A 90-day course requires 90 × 26 = 2340 nmol = 2.34 μmol total release. Feasibility: a 100 μL reservoir at 100 μM concentration = 10 nmol — INSUFFICIENT (need 2340 nmol). A 100 μL reservoir at 100 mM = 10 μmol — SUFFICIENT (4x margin). Conclusion: controlled release IS mathematically feasible if reservoir concentration is sufficiently high. This does NOT violate CE-003 (CSF turnover physics) because C3 uses CONTROLLED release (not membrane retention). G03 (CE constraints) PASSES. C3's mechanism is consistent with physics. However, this is an analytical derivation; experimental validation requires parameter sweep (C3-E04, blocked).
